lines.en: Hi there! **What can I start you with?**
lines.pt: Oi! Com o que posso começar para você?

lines.en: **Can I get a** cheeseburger **with** extra cheese?
lines.pt: Posso pedir um cheeseburger com queijo extra?

lines.en: Sure! **Do you want to make it a combo?** It comes with fries and a drink.
lines.pt: Claro! Quer fazer combo? Vem com batata frita e bebida.

lines.en: Yes, **make it a combo**, medium size.
**Without** onions, please. And a cola for the drink.
lines.pt: Sem cebola, por favor. E uma cola de bebida.

lines.en: No onions, one cola. **For here or to go?**
lines.pt: Sem cebola, uma cola. Para comer aqui ou levar?

lines.en: **To go**, please. How long is the wait?
lines.pt: Para levar, por favor. Quanto tempo demora?

lines.en: About five minutes. We’ll call your number.
lines.pt: Uns cinco minutos. Vamos chamar o seu número.

situation.text: You are hungry and in a hurry. You go to a fast-food counter, choose a combo, change one thing in your burger and say if the food is for here or to go.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can order a fast-food meal: choose a combo and a size, change an ingredient and say “for here” or “to go”.

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Life in the USA
pages.intro: Fast food is part of daily life in the USA. Look at the cards and guess the habit.

cards.note: A combo (or “meal”) is cheaper than buying each item alone.
You talk to a speaker, pay at one window and pick up at the next.
Many places have free refills for drinks if you eat inside.

levels.A1: A burger, fries and a drink.
levels.A2: A meal with a main item, fries and a drink.
levels.B1: A combo is a set meal that costs less than buying everything separately.
levels.B2: A combo bundles a main item, a side and a drink at a lower total price.

levels.A2: You stay in your car and get food at a window.
levels.B1: You order through a speaker, then pay and pick up the food from the car.
levels.B2: It is a service lane where you order, pay and collect food without leaving your car.

qs.q: What do you say at the end of the order?
qs.pt: O que você diz no fim do pedido?

levels.A2: For here or to go? To go, please.
levels.B1: I answer the question: for here or to go.
levels.B2: The cashier asks “For here or to go?” and I answer so they can pack it correctly.

pages.compare: In Brazil many people say “é pra comer aqui ou pra levar?” too. What is the order process in a fast-food place where you live?

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — natural American English
pages.tip: In a choice question the voice goes UP on the first option and DOWN on the last: “For HERE ↗ or to GO ↘?”

opts: For here or to go? (a choice)
For here? Or to go? (two questions)
For here, or to go. (a statement)

own.prompt: Write your own choice question: a drink, a size or a food.
own.criteria: Voice up on the first option, down on the last. Say it twice.

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: You do not need six different methods: the structure stays, while language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.say: Can I get a burger combo, no onions, to go?
I’d like the chicken sandwich, but could you leave off the mayo?
I think my order is missing the fries. Could you check, please?
I hate to bother you, but this isn’t what I ordered. Could we sort it out?
Forgive the trouble, but I’d appreciate it if the order could be set right.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.
